name: Place ID (Overture)
plain: A long code that identifies the place in Overture Maps. Use it to find the same place in Overture's own data.
definition: The Overture Maps identifier of the listing the observatory kept for the place: a 36-character code. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 31,536 places have one and all are different. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Copied from the Overture record. When duplicate listings are folded into one place, the kept listing's ID is published and the IDs of the folded listings are not.
how_to_read: Treat it as a label. The code says nothing about the place itself.
caveats: Overture sets its own rules for how an ID carries from one release to the next. Read Overture's documentation before you match the 2026-10 snapshot to another release.

The map's pop-ups do not show the ID. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places. That CSV holds the places that pass your current filters.

name: Place name
plain: The name Overture lists for the place, as its sources wrote it. A place the map does not draw has no name in the file.
definition: Overture's primary name for the listing. Every place the map draws has one; the 1,005 places it does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn). In the 2026-10 snapshot, the file holds 28,775 different names for 31,536 places, because chains such as fast-food brands have many outlets.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Copied from the Overture record (names.primary). The observatory does not translate names, fix spelling or change capital letters. It removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name (4 names held a telephone number in the 2026-10 snapshot).
how_to_read: The map search matches names. Two places can share a name, so use the place ID or the coordinates to tell them apart.
caveats: Some names carry extra words that a source added, such as a town or the country (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 537 names contain 'Puerto Rico' in any capital letters, for example 'Jardín Japonés, Ponce, Puerto Rico').
Spanish and English spellings both occur, so one place can be listed under different names. The observatory folds only some of these as duplicates.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 353 names start or end with a blank space (351 end with one and 2 start with one), because the observatory does not clean names. Trim them before you match or join on name.

Names are copied as written, except that a telephone number or an email address is removed. A listing named only after a private person, or by a street address, and a holiday rental are not drawn and have no name in the file; a few names may still look like the names of individual professionals who run a business. Check a name before you republish it outside the observatory.

name: Latitude and longitude of the place
plain: The position of the place's pin on the map, as latitude and longitude.
definition: Latitude and longitude of the listing's point, in decimal degrees (WGS 84, the World Geodetic System 1984 that GPS (Global Positioning System) and web maps use), rounded to 6 decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, latitudes run from 17.884134 to 18.515153 and longitudes from -67.940187 to -65.227658. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have no coordinates in the file (see Counted but not drawn).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Copied from the Overture record's point and rounded to 6 decimals. Every flag in the file (municipality, barrio, flood zone, protected area, land-use class and transit distance) is computed from this point.
how_to_read: The pin is where a source says the place is. It can sit on the street, at an entrance or in the middle of a lot.
caveats: Six decimals show the precision of the number, not the accuracy of the position. The source decides how accurate the pin is, and the observatory does not check it on the ground.
A place is one point. A beach, a river or a park appears as one pin, not as its shape or length.
Because every flag uses the pin, a pin a few meters off can change a flag, for example when it sits near the edge of a flood zone or a barrio.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,012 of the 31,536 places with a pin (6.4%) share an exact pin with at least one other place, at 614 locations (up to 23 places on one pin). The distance-based flags treat such places as being at the same spot, and the map groups close pins into clusters, so the pins you can see are fewer than the places.

name: Listed with a website
plain: Whether Overture lists a website for the place. The web address itself is not published.
definition: true when the Overture record lists a website; missing otherwise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 9,416 of 32,541 places (28.9%) are true, and 7,210 of 24,209 places on the default basis (29.8%).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Set by the build from the first website of the Overture record (websites[0]). The web address is not written to the file: the observatory publishes no business contact detail (owner rule of 2026-10-18; see Fields the observatory does not publish). Until 2026-10-18 the file published the address itself. A value that held an email address counts as no website (1 case in the 2026-10 snapshot).
how_to_read: A website means at least one source lists an online address for the place. It does not mean the place is open, that the site works or that it is the business's own site. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship. The Municipality tab counts these places once the listings are loaded; before that it shows with_website from municipalities.json.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot as first built (35,118 places, before 2026-10-18), many listed websites were not a business's own site: 886 (9.1%) were Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or X (Twitter) pages, 175 were Google Maps or goo.gl short links and 28 were WhatsApp links. The count of places with a website is therefore not a count of places with their own site.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, the municipal figure with_website adds up to the same 7,210 places on the default basis. Before 2026-10-18 it was one more than this field (7,441 against 7,440), because one website was counted before an email address was removed from it; that listing is no longer counted.

name: Counted but not drawn: the reason
plain: Why a place is counted in its municipality but not shown on the map: a holiday rental, or a rented unit named by its street address or unit number. Homes, housing and care services are not tourism and are not in the file at all (since 2026-10-18).
definition: One of two reasons, present only on places the map does not draw: holiday_rental (a holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays) and address (the name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground, or as a business such as a restaurant). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,005 of 32,541 places are withheld (holiday_rental 971, address 34), and 742 of them are among the 24,209 places on the default basis (holiday_rental 715, address 27). Three more reasons, residence (a private home, or a listing named after a private person), residential (a residential building, condominium, housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation) and sensitive (an elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice and similar), and an address-named listing filed where homes are filed, mean the listing is not tourism: since 2026-10-18 it is left out of the file and of every count (HANDOFF decision 47). That left out 2,577 listings (residential 2,301, residence 157, address 67, sensitive 52), 2,370 of them on the default basis.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: places_privacy.py decides from the Overture category and the name, with a reviewed list of exceptions (places_review.json): a sensitive word or a street address in the name withholds a place in any category; home words (Casa, Residencia, Hacienda, Villa...) and housing words (Urb., Residencial, Condominio, Apartments...) withhold it in the categories where Meta users file homes (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar), unless the name also names an accommodation business or a public venue; and a lodging listing must name an accommodation. Holiday rentals (owner decision of 2026-10-18, HANDOFF decision 48) are withheld by category (holiday rental home, cabin, cottage, service apartment) and, in the lodging categories, by a name that says so (Vacation Rental, Beach House, Airbnb, Short Term Rental, Tiny House, ... Rentals, ... Stays) and, in the hotel, B&B, hostel and campground categories, by a name that rents a unit (... Apartment, Casita ..., Penthouse ..., Studio, Bungalow, Cabin, Chalet, Cottage, Villa 12, ... House, ... Home, ... Villa), a run of units (... Apartments, Condominio ...) or a house called Casa or Villa and one word, alone or followed by a town, municipio or neighborhood, unless the name also names a hotel, guest house, inn, B&B, hostel, posada, parador or resort; hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs stay drawn, and real guest houses, hostels and aparthotels with such names are drawn by review. A home word followed by a unit or house number (Casa ... 28) withholds a place in any category. A listing withheld as residence, residential or sensitive, or as address in a category where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar; a numbered holiday rental there is recorded as holiday_rental), is not tourism and is dropped before every count (places_privacy.not_tourism, decision 47 of 2026-10-18). A listing whose name also says holiday rental is recorded as holiday_rental (counted, not drawn) unless the name says housing clearly: a subdivision or estate word (Urb., Residencial, Estancias, Villas de...), a condominium or apartment building named as such (Condominio, Edificio, Torre), or a neighborhood, sector or barrio of the gazetteer within 3 km. Outside the lodging category, Edificio, Edif. and Building alone do not say housing. A withheld place keeps the fields the counts use (municipality, barrio, category, type, Overture category, confidence, source, flood, protected-area, land-use and transit fields) and loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date; its confidence is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's filter, and its distances to a stop and departures (transit_m here, ts_m, tw_m, ts_calls and tw_calls in place_access.json) to one value per class, so every count stays the same. The withheld rows come after all the drawn ones, sorted by their own fields, because Overture's order follows location. hub_400m (true or missing, only on a withheld place) says whether a rail station or ferry terminal is within 400 m, so the nightly transit refresh can still count the place. Owner rule of 2026-10-18; guide: docs/places-privacy.md.
how_to_read: These places are in every count and share (the Municipality tab, the choropleths of places shown, municipalities.json, barrios.geojson). They are not pins, hexagons, search results, list rows or CSV rows. They are tourism supply: 3.1% of the counted places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Until 2026-10-18 the counts also included the homes, housing and care services that Overture's sources filed under tourism categories: 2,370 of the 26,579 places then counted (8.9%). Since then they are left out, and every count and share was rebuilt without them (decision 47).
caveats: Overture gives no ownership or use field. The patterns can miss a home or hold back a public place; places_review.json lists the reviewed exceptions with their reasons.
A withheld place keeps the transit distances of the last full build: the nightly refresh cannot measure it again without its point.

values.holiday_rental: A holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays, by its Overture category or a name that says so (971 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs are drawn.
values.residence: A private home, or a listing named only after a private person. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (157 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.residential: A residential building, condominium, public housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (2,301 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.address: The name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground (a numbered unit rented to visitors) or as a business (34). The same names filed where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar) are numbered homes and flats: not tourism, left out since 2026-10-18 (67).
values.sensitive: An elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice, a care, foster or recovery home (including one named 'Hogar ...' and filed under a lodging category) or a similar service. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (52 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot). The observatory publishes treatment facilities as counts only (community_series.json).

name: Municipality of the place
plain: The municipio where the place's pin sits, using Census boundaries. It can differ from the town named in the address.
definition: The name of one of Puerto Rico's 78 municipalities, spelled with accents (for example Bayamón or Mayagüez). Every place has one.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against Census municipality boundaries that are generalized and clipped to the shoreline. A pin that falls in no boundary takes the municipality whose boundary is nearest (muni_locate.py); in the 2026-10 snapshot it took the nearest municipality center. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
source_detail: Overture places; US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries (500k, shoreline-clipped, Generalized_ACS2023 service); municipality centers from the observatory's own list of 78 municipalities.
how_to_read: Use it to count or compare places by municipality. Every count of places per municipality in the observatory uses this field. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the address names a different municipality than the one the pin falls in for 863 places (2.7% of the file). 325 places have no town in the address, and 590 more have a town text that is not one of the 78 municipality names.

Pins just offshore or at the shoreline can fall outside every boundary polygon. In the 2026-10 snapshot that is 348 places (1.1%). The 2026-10 build gave them the nearest municipality center, which can differ from the municipality next to the pin; the next full build gives them the nearest boundary, which moves 60 of them.
Boundaries are the Census Bureau's generalized lines, not legal survey lines.

A count of places is not a rate. Larger and more populous municipalities have more places: in the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has 3,424 places on the default basis and Maricao 36. To compare municipalities, use places per 1,000 residents or per km2. A rate per resident is high where visitors are many compared with residents.

name: Barrio of the place
plain: The barrio where the place's pin sits. A barrio is a sub-municipal district that the Census Bureau calls a county subdivision. Only places counted by default have one.
definition: The name of the Census barrio (the Census Bureau calls it a county subdivision) that contains the pin. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,884 places have one: every place on the default basis except 325. Places of worship and places below the confidence cut have none.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Point-in-polygon test against Census barrio boundaries, run only for places counted by default (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship). The first matching polygon is used. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county subdivisions (barrios), 500k, shoreline-clipped; field BASENAME.
how_to_read: Always read the barrio together with the municipality. Many barrio names repeat: in the barrio layer of the 2026-10 snapshot, 133 of the 694 barrio names occur in more than one municipality (for example Collores or Playa). Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio because their pin falls in no barrio polygon. Almost all of them (323) are also outside the shoreline municipality polygons, that is offshore or at the shoreline.
The barrio is the Census Bureau's subdivision. It is not always the neighborhood name people use.
The place pop-up does not show the barrio. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places.

name: Tourism category
plain: The tourism group a place belongs to: Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations or Visitor services.
definition: One of four codes set by the observatory from the place's Overture category: ATTRACTIONS, GASTRONOMY, ACCOMMODATIONS or VISITOR_SERVICES. The map writes the last one as Visitor Services. Places of worship are filed under ATTRACTIONS.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Ordered text rules read the Overture category and its parent groups. See 'How Overture categories become tourism categories'.
how_to_read: Use it to filter places and to compare the mix of supply. Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set the four groups. They are not an official or industry classification. Each place has one category and one type. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places of worship (5,032 listings) carry the code ATTRACTIONS but are left out of counts by default.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, Gastronomy is the largest group by a wide margin: 19,429 of 32,541 places in the file (60%). Keep that in mind when you compare groups.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

name: Place type
plain: The more specific kind of place, such as Beaches, Restaurants or Hotels. The 2026-10 snapshot has 27 types under the four categories.
definition: One of the 27 type names that occur in the 2026-10 snapshot, set by the observatory from the place's Overture category. Each type belongs to one category. Two more type names appear in the observatory's rules or on the map legend, but no place carries them in that snapshot: Food Markets (Gastronomy) and Landmarks (Attractions).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Ordered text rules, applied to the Overture category and its parent groups. The first rule that matches decides the type, and then the place's Overture group can override it. See 'How Overture categories become tourism categories'.
how_to_read: Types appear in map pop-ups, in a municipality's list of top types and in search. A type is a rule-based label, so read the type's own entry to see what it includes and leaves out. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: Several types are broader or narrower than their names. For example Historic Sites includes many residential buildings, Marinas holds boat businesses, and, in the 2026-10 snapshot, Cultural Experience Providers holds only dance studios.
The place counts in this entry, including those in the table of codes, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.Places of Worship: Attractions. Churches and other places of worship; not counted by default. 5,032 places in the file, 0 on the default basis.

source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1 (downloaded 1 October 2026); taxonomy.primary and taxonomy.hierarchy (basic_category if there is no primary), sorted into FPR's types by the observatory's classification rules.

name: Overture category (original)
plain: The category Overture gave the place, such as restaurant, beach or hotel. The observatory keeps it so you can see how each place was classified.
definition: Overture's primary category for the listing: lowercase words joined by underscores. 265 different values occur in the 2026-10 snapshot (268 before the listings that are not tourism were left out on 2026-10-18). The observatory uses it, with the parent groups above it in Overture's category tree, to set the category and type.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Copied from the Overture record (taxonomy.primary, or basic_category when the primary is missing). The map pop-up shows it with the underscores replaced by spaces.
how_to_read: Use it to check or redo the classification: find the code below, then the rule words in the type's entry. The same Overture category can land in a different type when its parent group differs; in the 2026-10 snapshot every code maps to one type.
caveats: The category names and their meaning are Overture's. Overture can rename or add categories between releases.
Some records carry only one of Overture's broad group names (arts_and_entertainment, geographic_entities, food_and_drink, lodging) instead of a specific category.
The place counts in this entry, including those in the table of codes, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

A few codes sit under an unexpected type because of the text rules. See the notes on trailer_dealer, airport_lounge, marina, the religious codes and the food shops (candy_store, chocolatier, delicatessen).

name: Overture confidence score
plain: Overture's own score, from 0 to 1, for a listing. The map's Map layers tab describes it as Overture's estimate that a listing is a real, current place. The observatory counts places at 0.50 or higher by default.
definition: A number from 0 to 1 with three decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it runs from 0.024 to 1.000, the middle value is 0.83, 128 places score exactly 1, 14 score exactly 0.50 and 3,574 (11.0%) score below 0.50.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Copied from the Overture record and rounded to 3 decimals. Each record names an Overture 'confidence calculation' as the source of this value. In the 2026-10 snapshot, for 30,817 places (94.7%) it equals the score on the record from the contributing source (mostly Meta), and for the other 1,724 it differs. The observatory does not change it, except on a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn): there the score is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's confidence filter (0.57 is written 0.55), so every count at every filter setting is the same and the exact score is not published. The figures in the definition are for the scores Overture gives.
source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1 (downloaded 1 October 2026); field confidence. The Overture documentation (docs.overturemaps.org/guides/places/) explains how the score is built. The confidence-calculation entry on each record has version 2026-09-17.
how_to_read: A higher score means Overture is more confident in the listing. It is an estimate, not a rating of quality and not a measure of how many people visit.
caveats: The observatory does not check places on the ground, so a high score does not prove that a place is open today. The map's Map layers tab describes the score as an estimate that a listing is a real, current place.
The observatory's default cut at 0.50 is its own choice, not an Overture rule. See 'Which places the observatory counts'.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 3,574 listings below 0.50 are Meta records (11.2% of Meta's 31,945). No Foursquare, Microsoft or AllThePlaces record scores below 0.50, so the cut filters only Meta records.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, scores look different by source: 251 of 252 Foursquare places score exactly 0.77, 137 of 241 Microsoft places score 0.85 and 77 of 103 AllThePlaces places score 0.80, while Meta scores take 948 different values. The score does not rank places within those three sources.
The cut also removes more places of some types than others. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 0.50 cut removes 27% of Vacation Properties and 3% of Beaches.

name: FEMA flood zone at the place
plain: The flood zone that FEMA (the US Federal Emergency Management Agency) maps at the place's pin. It is shown only when the pin is in a mapped high-risk area (1% annual chance of flooding) or in the 0.2% annual chance area.
definition: The FEMA flood zone code of the flood-map polygon that contains the pin. It is published only for places inside a Special Flood Hazard Area (the zones that occur in the 2026-10 snapshot are A, AE, AO, A99 and VE) or inside the shaded 0.2% annual chance zone (zone X with that subtype). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 7,266 of 32,541 places have one (22.3%).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the flood polygons of the National Flood Hazard Layer for Puerto Rico, which FEMA publishes. The observatory skips polygons marked open water or area not included (the 2026-10 download has none). When a pin lies in overlapping polygons, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone. Unshaded zone X (minimal hazard) is not recorded. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
source_detail: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, MapServer layer 28 (flood hazard zones), polygons with DFIRM_ID starting with 72 (Puerto Rico); fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY and SFHA_TF.
how_to_read: Zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and VE all mean a 1% chance of flooding in any given year, often called the 100-year flood. A 1% annual chance does not mean one flood every 100 years. It is a 1-in-100 chance each year, and it repeats every year. X with the 0.2% subtype is the 500-year area. A place with no flood zone is in neither mapped area. That does not mean it cannot flood.
caveats: This is the mapped hazard at one point. It does not describe the building, its floor height or its insurance.

Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
FEMA revises its maps. The 2026-10 snapshot used the layer as downloaded on 1 October 2026.
The descriptions in the codes below are plain-language summaries. The FEMA definitions are the reference.
FEMA's printed Flood Insurance Rate Map and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. This is a database copy and not a flood determination for any property.
The file does not carry the effective date of the flood map at each place. The observatory downloads only the fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF and STATIC_BFE.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

definition: Meters from the place's map point to the nearest scheduled stop whose operator's timetable feed has an end date on or after the as-of date (the field as_of of place_access.json). Stops of feeds that have ended, stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. The distance is rounded up to whole meters, so a value of 400 or less is exactly the test behind the shares of places near a stop with a current timetable. 99,999 is the largest value the file can hold. The file has one value for each place of places.json, in the same order. It carries no place ids, so a page joins the two files by position and checks that its count n equals the number of places and that the build time in its field built matches generated_at in meta.json. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class: 400 (400 m or less), 800 (more than 400, up to 800), 1000 (more than 800, up to 1,000) or 99,999 (more than 1,000); every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).

The as-of date is the build date at a full build and the run date in the nightly refresh. name: How Overture categories become tourism categories
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: The observatory reads each Overture category and files the place under one of four tourism categories and one type within it (27 types occur in the 2026-10 snapshot). Places that fit none of them are left out, and so are listings that fit a category but are not tourism: homes, housing and care services (since 2026-10-18).
definition: A set of 28 ordered text rules plus a mapping of Overture's top-level groups, both set by the observatory's build script (the tourism taxonomy of Foundation for Puerto Rico). Overture sorts its categories in a tree, and the top level is called a group here (for example food_and_drink). The rules look for words inside Overture's category names, so a match is by text, not by an official code list.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The observatory tests each listing's Overture category name against 28 ordered text rules, and then the listing's Overture group can override the result. The five steps and the 28 rules are listed below.
how_to_read: Read the rules as a ladder: the first match wins, and then the Overture group can override it. When a result looks odd, find the place's Overture category in the Overture category entry, then the rule words in the type's entry.
caveats: The rules match words inside longer words. For example the word trail also matches trailer dealers (6 places in Scenic Areas in the 2026-10 snapshot).

Rule order changes results. Amusement parks and water parks are filed as Parks, bar-and-grill restaurants as Bars, and beach resorts as Lodging. Rental businesses outside the lodging group are not kept, because the word rental matches a Vacation Properties rule before the Transportation or Marinas rule. So the keywords car_rental, bike_rental and scooter_rental in rule 27 never decide a result.
The word plaza in rule 9 does not keep a listing by itself. In the 2026-10 snapshot, public plazas (114) were left out because Overture does not file them under an attractions group.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 63,117 of 99,323 Overture places are left out (63.5%), among them 3,388 with no category. After duplicates are folded, 2,577 more listings that fit a category are left out because they are not tourism (homes, housing estates, condominiums and care services; see Counted but not drawn). The most common left-out categories are beauty salon (3,167), grocery store (1,478), professional service (1,419), automotive repair (1,419), doctors office (1,280), auto dealer (1,279), gas station (1,250), spa (1,189). Some visitor-related categories are also left out: travel service (295), car rental service (174), travel and transportation with no finer category (146), public plazas (114), farmers markets (61), souvenir stores (53), boat rental and training (23), flea markets (22), travel companies (19), train stations (18), airlines (18), jet skis rental (14), golf courses (13), all-terrain vehicle (ATV) rental tours (9), motorcycle rental service (8) and bike rental (7). Visitor services counts do not include these businesses.

Food Markets is a defined type with no places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Gastronomy is accepted only for listings in Overture's food_and_drink group, and grocery stores and farmers markets sit in Overture's shopping group.
Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set this grouping. It is not an official or industry classification.
The counts in this entry are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.Step 1: Take the category name: Take Overture's primary category for the listing, or its basic category when there is no primary. A listing with neither is left out.
values.Step 2: Test the rules: Test that category name against the 28 rules in order: Attractions rules first, then Gastronomy, Accommodations and Visitor services. The first rule that matches gives a category and a type. If no rule matches the name, test the full category path (the group and parent names joined) the same way.
values.Step 3: Find the Overture group: Find the listing's Overture group: the first of lodging, food_and_drink, cultural_and_historic, arts_and_entertainment or geographic_entities in its path (the rules also recognize the older names accommodation, eat_and_drink and attractions_and_activities). Lodging maps to Accommodations, food_and_drink to Gastronomy and the other three to Attractions.
values.Step 4: Let the group decide: If the listing has such a group, keep it. When the rule's category equals the group's category, the rule's type is used. Otherwise the group's category is used with its default type: Lodging, Restaurants or Tourist Attractions.
values.Step 5: Listings with no group: If the listing has no such group, keep it only when a rule puts it in Visitor services, or in Beaches, Nature Reserves, Scenic Areas, Historic Sites, Museums, Parks or Places of Worship. Everything else is left out.
values.Rule 1: Places of Worship: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains place_of_worship, church, cathedral, chapel, synagogue, mosque, temple or religious.
values.Rule 2: Beaches: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name starts with beach.
values.Rule 3: Parks: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name is exactly park, ends with _park, starts with park_, or contains playground, national_park or state_park.
values.Rule 4: Nature Reserves: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains nature, forest, wildlife, reserve or botanical.
values.Rule 5: Museums: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains museum.
values.Rule 6: Historic Sites: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains historic, monument, fort, castle or ruin.
values.Rule 7: Cultural Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains art_gallery, theater, theater, performing_arts, cultural_center, cinema or movie_theater.
values.Rule 8: Scenic Areas: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains scenic, lookout, viewpoint, waterfall, cave, lake, river, island, mountain, hiking_trail or trail.
values.Rule 9: Tourist Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains tourist, attraction, amusement, zoo, aquarium, water_park, theme_park, observatory, plaza or landmark.
values.Rule 10: Bakeries: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains bakery, pastry, patisserie or donut.
values.Rule 11: Cafes: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains cafe, coffee, tea_room, ice_cream, dessert, juice_bar or bubble_tea.
values.Rule 12: Nightlife: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains night_club, nightclub, karaoke, lounge, dance_club or live_music.
values.Rule 13: Bars: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains the word bar on its own, ends with _bar, starts with bar_, ends with pub, or contains brewery, brewpub, beer_garden, cocktail, sports_bar or wine_bar.

name: Which places the observatory counts (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship)
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: Unless you change the filter, the observatory counts a place only when Overture's confidence score is 0.50 or higher and it is not a place of worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, that gives 24,209 tourism places.
definition: The default basis is: confidence of 0.50 or higher, and a type other than Places of Worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, of the 32,541 places in the file, 5,032 are places of worship and 3,300 more score below 0.50, which leaves 24,209. In this entry a listing is one record about a place in Overture's data (name, location, category, source), and a pin is the point on the map where a place's coordinates sit. After duplicates are folded, the observatory keeps one listing for each place.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The observatory's build sets the minimum confidence to 0.50. The place counts and shares in municipalities.json (assets, by_category, in_sfha, in_flood_zone, in_protected, with_website, avg_confidence, sfha_pct, places_near_transit, transit_pct, access_n, the acc_ shares and the per-resident and per-km2 rates) and every count in barrios.geojson use that basis. Three exceptions: assets_all_confidence and listings_all, which are meant to show other bases, and places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct, which count every listing in the file that has a land-use class (32,369 of 32,541 in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and places below 0.50. meta.json records the cut as min_confidence. The 2D map starts at the same value: the Minimum confidence slider runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05, and the Include places of worship box starts off. The 3D view always uses 0.50 and hides places of worship. A place that scores exactly 0.50 is counted.
how_to_read: Use the slider when you want a stricter or looser list. On a municipality profile, the place count, flood share, protected share, website count and transit share follow your filters. Places per 1,000 residents, places per km2 and the ranks always use the default basis, so they can disagree with the count beside them. The CSV (comma-separated values) of one municipality's places follows your filters. The CSV of all municipalities (rankings and shading) uses the default basis. In the 2026-10 snapshot, a basis with no confidence cut and no worship holds 27,509 places.
caveats: The 0.50 cut is the observatory's own choice, not an Overture rule.
The cut matters. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory counts 24,209 places at 0.50. With no cut and no places of worship it would count 27,509.
The cut removes more places of some types than others, and in the 2026-10 snapshot all 3,574 places below 0.50 are Meta records. See the confidence score entry.
The municipal land-use place shares (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct) do not follow this basis.
Folding duplicates can also remove places from the default count. See the duplicates entry.

name: How duplicate listings are folded
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: When several listings look like the same place, the observatory keeps the one with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. In the 2026-10 snapshot, this folded 1,088 listings.
definition: Two listings count as the same place when they share a municipality (taken from the address town, see step 1) and a category, sit close together, and have alike names (or the same phone number and somewhat alike names). Matches chain: if A matches B and B matches C, all three become one place.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The build groups listings by municipality and category, compares nearby pairs, and joins pairs whose names are alike. It keeps the listing with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. The steps are listed below.
how_to_read: A place with a duplicates value above 0 stands for several listings. The map pop-up shows the count. Rankings and counts use the kept listing only.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, most groups are small: 574 of the 691 places with folded listings have exactly one.

A few groups are large. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the two largest groups (43 and 36 folded listings) are built on neighborhood names (Condado and Isla Verde) and mix beaches, parks, condominiums and other places that share the name. The kept listing is only one of them.
Folded listings can have different types (for example a beach and a park), and the type of the kept listing is the one published. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 290 groups mix types.
Listings in different municipalities or different categories are never compared, so some real duplicates remain.
The step runs before the confidence cut and before the municipality is set from the pin, so a low-confidence listing can be folded into a higher one, and the group uses the address town.

Folding can remove places from the default count. It is done within a category, not a type, and the highest-confidence listing is kept. Places of worship share the Attractions category, so in the 2026-10 snapshot 74 listings of other types (67 with confidence 0.50 or higher) were folded into a kept place of worship, which is not counted by default. The other way round, 19 places of worship were folded into a kept listing of another type. These figures come from re-running the folding step on the Overture release used for that snapshot, for the places in the file.

values.Step 1: Group listings: Same municipality and same category. The municipality here is the address town when it names one of the 78 municipalities (accents and capital letters ignored). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, 325 have no address town and 590 have a town text that is not a municipality name.
values.Step 2: Compare pairs: Pairs within 1,000 m if either listing is a Beach, Park, Nature Reserve, Scenic Area, Historic Site or Tourist Attraction; within 600 m for all other types.
values.Step 3: Same place when: The name similarity is 0.95 or more; or it is 0.80 or more and the listings are within 600 m (those natural types) or 150 m (all other types); or the listings share the same phone number, the similarity is 0.50 or more and they are within 500 m.
values.Step 4: Chain the matches: Matching pairs are joined into groups. If A matches B and B matches C, all three are one place.
values.Step 5: Keep one: The listing with the highest confidence is kept. Ties go to the listing with more contact details on file (website, phone, email, address), then to the one with more social links. The duplicates field is the group size minus 1.
values.Name similarity: Names are compared as sets of words. Accents and capital letters are ignored, words shorter than 3 letters are dropped, and common words are dropped (for example the, de, playa, hotel, restaurante, church and the names of the 78 municipalities). The two names must share a word of 4 letters or more. The score is the shared words divided by all words, or, when the shorter name has two or more words (or both names are short), the shared words divided by the shorter name's words times 0.9, whichever is higher.

name: How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: The municipality comes from where the map pin sits, tested against Census boundaries. The barrio comes from the same kind of test against Census barrio boundaries.
definition: The municipality and the barrio are set from the pin, not from the address text. The address town is used only while duplicate listings are folded.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Step 1 (used only to fold duplicates): the municipality is the address town when it matches one of the 78 municipality names (ignoring accents and capital letters). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. Step 2 (published): after folding, each pin is tested against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipality polygons. The polygon that contains the pin gives the municipality. Step 3: a pin that is inside no polygon (offshore, or at a gap in the shoreline) takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the nearest municipality center). Step 4: for places counted by default only (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship), the pin is tested against the Census barrio polygons. The first polygon that contains it gives the barrio.
source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries and county subdivisions (500k, shoreline-clipped); municipality centers from the observatory's own list.
how_to_read: The published municipality is where the pin is, so counts agree with the boundaries drawn on the map. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 863 places have an address town that names another municipality. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 348 places fall in no municipality polygon and took the nearest center. For example, one beach pin on Mona Island falls outside every polygon and took Rincón, while the other three listings on the island are in Mayagüez. The next full build gives such a pin the nearest polygon instead, which puts that beach in Mayagüez too.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio, and places of worship and places below the confidence cut never get one.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the barrio layer has 901 polygons and 694 different names, so a barrio name alone can point to several municipalities.

name: How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: Flood zone, protected area, land-use class, barrio and municipality are set by checking which map polygon contains the place's pin. Transit access is the distance to the nearest mapped stop and to the nearest stop with a current timetable.
definition: Each flag is a spatial test of the pin (latitude and longitude) against another dataset. Nothing is read from the place's name, address or category.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The build checks whether the pin lies inside a polygon of each of these datasets: FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood polygons (flood zone, subtype and Special Flood Hazard Area flag), PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) polygons (protected area and GAP (Gap Analysis Project) status), the land-use plan polygons (land use and group), Census barrio polygons (barrio) and Census municipality polygons (municipality). A pin exactly on a polygon's edge does not count as inside. Where polygons overlap, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone for flood; the lowest GAP number wins for protected areas, and proclamation boundaries are ignored; the first polygon found is used for land use and barrio. The tests use the polygons at the detail the sources give them, not the simplified copies drawn on the map. Transit is different: access.py finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind and stores its distance, its name and the 400 m flag in places.json (see places.transit_m), and finds the nearest stop with a current timetable, which it stores in place_access.json (see place_access.ts_m).
how_to_read: Read each flag as 'the dataset says this about the spot where the pin is'. It is not a finding about the building or the lot.
caveats: The result depends on how accurate the pin is and on how detailed and how current each polygon dataset is. A pin near an edge can fall on either side.
Only one value is kept per field, even when several polygons overlap the pin.
The Census boundaries are generalized by the Census Bureau, so pins close to the coast or to a boundary can fall on the other side of the true line.

name: Fields the observatory does not publish
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: The observatory does not publish the phone, email, social-media links, street address, website, postcode, brand name or source license label of an Overture record, and it removes a telephone number written into a name.
definition: Eight fields of Overture's records are read by the build but never written to places.json: phone, email, socials (social-media links), address (the street address), website, postcode, brand (the brand name) and source_license (the license label of the contributing source). Only whether a website is listed is kept (has_website). The field region is not written either: the map works it out from the municipality. A place the map does not draw also loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date (see Counted but not drawn).
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The build removes these eight fields when it writes each place (places_privacy.py). Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. The counts of phone, website, email, address and social links decide which duplicate is kept. Postcode, brand and license label are read and dropped without use. The build also leaves out any field that is empty or false, and removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name. Until 2026-10-18 the street address and the website were published; the owner rule of that date is never to publish business contact details or any personal data.
how_to_read: Contact details of individual businesses can identify people, so the observatory leaves these fields out. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, the Overture record holds a phone number for 24,077 (74%), an email address for 12,711 (39%), social-media links for 32,104 (99%), a street address for 27,235 (84%), a website for 9,416 (29%), a postcode for 26,760 (82%) and a brand name for 1,963 (6%). Those fields are not in the observatory's data. Names are copied as the source wrote them, apart from a telephone number or an email address (see the caveats).
caveats: None of the eight fields is written to the published file. Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. Phone, website, email, address and social links are counted to decide which duplicate is kept.

Names are free text. A telephone number or an email address written into a name is removed (4 names in the 2026-10 snapshot); names are not otherwise scrubbed. The street addresses and websites published until 2026-10-18 held telephone numbers (at least 6 addresses, and 28 websites pointed to WhatsApp) and social-media pages that can belong to individuals; they are no longer published, but copies made before that date can still hold them.
CSV (comma-separated values) downloads from the map hold only the published fields.
The source license label is not published for each place. The labels per source are listed in the codes of the contributing data source entry.

name: How to read a missing value in the places file
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: A field that is empty for a place is left out of the file instead of being written as blank or false. So a missing flood zone, protected area or barrio means no value was found, not that the value is zero.
definition: The observatory does not write a field when its value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list. That is why the yes flags (sfha and transit_400m) appear only as true, and why optional fields appear on some places and not on others.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: The build removes every field whose value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list, when it writes each place. Numbers, including 0, are kept.
how_to_read: A missing value is not a measured zero and is not a promise of safety. Read the notes below for each field. In a spreadsheet, an empty cell means the same as a missing field.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot every place has category, type, overture_category, municipality, confidence, source, duplicates and transit_m, and every place the map draws also has oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop and updated. The build would leave out name, source or updated for a record that has none.

values.sfha: Missing means the pin was not found inside a Special Flood Hazard Area. Present only as true.
values.transit_400m: Missing means the nearest mapped stop of any kind is more than 400 m away. Present only as true.
values.flood_zone: Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
values.flood_subtype: Missing means the place has no flood zone, or its zone has no subtype.
values.protected_area: Missing means the pin is in no PAD-US area (proclamation boundaries do not count).
values.barrio: Missing means the place is not counted by default (worship or below the confidence cut), or its pin is in no barrio polygon.
values.land_use: Missing means the pin is in no land-use plan polygon (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 173 places; the largest groups are in San Juan, Fajardo, Culebra and Cabo Rojo, and all 4 places on Mona Island are among them).
values.has_website: Missing means no source gave a website, or the value held an email address. The web address itself is never published.
values.withheld: Missing means the map draws the place. Present on the places counted but not drawn, which also have no oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop or updated.
values.hub_400m: Present only as true, and only on a place the map does not draw.
values.duplicates: Never missing. A place with no folded listings shows 0.
values.transit_m: Never missing. A place at a stop shows 0.
values.ts_m, ts_calls and ts_we (place_access.j: Never missing: the file holds one value for each place, in the order of places.json. ts_calls 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m. ts_we 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m, or no Saturday or Sunday service in the published timetable. ts_m is 99,999 at most.

name: How the tourism places file is made
group: Tourism places: how the data are made
plain: The observatory takes the places that Overture Maps lists in Puerto Rico and keeps those that fit four tourism categories. It folds duplicates, adds location and hazard flags, and does not copy the phone, email or social-media fields.
definition: places.json is a list of 32,541 places built from 99,323 Overture records (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026). It is rebuilt with each snapshot of the observatory (Snapshot 2026-10 here). The file is a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) list in UTF-8 text with one object for each place and up to 23 fields per place (26 field names occur in the file). It is not GeoJSON: the position is in the separate fields lat and lng.
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities
method: Step 1: download every Overture place inside the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57 (all of Puerto Rico, including Mona, Culebra and Vieques) as GeoJSON points (99,323 records in the 2026-10 snapshot). Step 2: classify each record (see the classification entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 36,206 fit one of the four categories, and 63,117 are left out. Step 3: fold duplicates (see the duplicates entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,088 listings are folded into others, which leaves 35,118 listings. Then leave out the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services; see Counted but not drawn): 2,577 in the 2026-10 snapshot, which leaves 32,541 places (since 2026-10-18). Step 4: set the municipality from the pin position. Step 5: test each pin against the FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood zones, the PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) protected areas, the 2015 land-use plan, the transit stops and the barrio boundaries. Step 6: remove the phone, email, social-media, postcode, brand and license fields (see the unpublished fields entry), and write places.json.
source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026 and cut to the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57. The observatory's build is labeled Snapshot 2026-10.
how_to_read: The file is a snapshot of one Overture release. Places that opened, closed or moved after that release are not in it.
caveats: Coverage depends on what Overture's sources list. A place that no source lists is missing, and a place that has closed can still be listed. The observatory does not check places on the ground.

Licenses: Overture's place records carry the license of each contributing source. In the 2026-10 snapshot the labels are CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (Meta and Microsoft records), Apache-2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0-1.0 (AllThePlaces). Read Overture's terms and each source's terms before you reuse or redistribute the records.
The map credits Overture Maps Foundation contributors for place data.

Counts from two snapshots are not comparable as a time series. A new Overture release can add or drop listings from its sources without any business opening or closing, and the observatory does not track openings and closures.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, coverage follows Meta's: 98.2% of the places (31,945 of 32,541) list Meta as the source, so the mix of categories mostly reflects what Meta lists.

name: Walking distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (m)
plain: How far a tourism place is from the nearest stop whose published timetable has not ended, walking along mapped roads. It is the distance behind the access class in the map pop-up. It is an estimate: the road map has no footpaths or sidewalks.
definition: Meters walked from the place's map point to the nearest scheduled stop whose operator's timetable feed has an end date on or after the as-of date (as_of in place_access.json), along the roads of site/data/roads.bin except motorways and motorway links. A scheduled stop is a stop in the timetable feed (GTFS) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or of a municipal transit system; ended feeds, volunteer-mapped stops, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. The distance is rounded up to whole meters, so a value of 400 or less is exactly the test behind the walking shares. The search stops at 1,000 m (walk_bound_m in the file): 99,999 means no such stop within a 1,000 m walk. A place with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its straight-line distance (ts_m) and is listed in tw_straight. The file has one value for each place of places.json, in the same order, joined by position like ts_m. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class: 400 (400 m or less), 800 (more than 400, up to 800), 1000 (more than 800, up to the 1,000 m bound) or 99,999 (beyond the bound); a place in tw_straight takes the coarsened ts_m; every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
unit: meters (walked along mapped roads, rounded up)
geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities (32,541 places)

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py), from the road file the site publishes (roads.bin); the file is rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the stops were read on 2026-10-02 and the access is as of 2026-10-06 (as_of in the file).

method: walknet.py builds a walking network from site/data/roads.bin: every road except motorways and motorway links, usable in both directions. Each place and each stop with a current timetable is joined to the nearest walkable road within 150 m by a straight connector. access.py then searches the network from every such stop, up to 1,000 m (a bounded Dijkstra search), so the walking distance is connector + path along the roads + connector. Distances use the observatory's flat-earth formula on a plane centered on Puerto Rico, the same scale as ts_m. A walk is never shorter than the straight line, so tw_m is at least ts_m. Two cases fall back to the straight line so that nothing is silently dropped: a place with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its ts_m (it is listed in tw_straight), and a stop with no walkable road within 150 m (12 of 2,881 in the 2026-10 snapshot) counts at its straight-line distance.
source_detail: Place coordinates: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026), tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR). Stops: scheduled stops in transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02). Feed end dates: operators.json. Roads: OpenStreetMap (roads.py builds site/data/roads.bin from the Geofabrik extract; ODbL).
how_to_read: A smaller number means a shorter walk to a stop whose timetable is still in force. 400 or less is a stop within a 400 m walk; 401 to 800 is the 'Stop 400–800 m away' class of the pop-up; 99,999 means more than 1,000 m. Compare it with ts_m: the walk is a median 1.43 times the straight line where both are measured (90th percentile 2.43). In the 2026-10 snapshot 9,042 of the 32,541 places are within a 400 m walk, and so are 6,787 of the 24,209 places on the default basis (28.0%, against 32.2% in a straight line). 1,003 places on the default basis are within 400 m in a straight line but not on foot.
caveats: Along mapped roads, not every way a person can walk. The road file has no footways, paths, steps, pedestrian streets, sidewalks or crossings, and it does not know fences, gates or a road that is unsafe to cross. The visitor-access study (docs/analysis/visitor-access-2026-10) repeated the run on a full OpenStreetMap walking network: the island share within 400 m moved from 26.6% to 27.0%, and municipal shares moved a median 0.0 points (90th percentile 0.99, largest 11.3 in Hormigueros).

1,210 places (1,074 on the default basis, 4.4%) have no walkable road within 150 m and keep their straight-line distance (see place_access.tw_straight). For them the value is a lower bound: the real walk is at least that long.

Motorways and motorway links are left out because pedestrians cannot use them. A footbridge or underpass that the road file does not hold is missed, so a place across a motorway from a stop can read farther than it is.

Large grounds with no mapped public road inside (the airport, malls, resorts, campuses) make long detours. In the 2026-10 snapshot Carolina drops from 88.5% to 70.7% of places within 400 m, much of it around the airport and Plaza Carolina.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. A timetable is a schedule: it does not show that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
The values change on the day a feed ends. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed (see methods.access_profile).
Each distance starts at the place's listed point, which can be wrong in the source (Overture Maps).

name: Weekday calls at the busiest stop with a current timetable within a 400 m walk
plain: The most scheduled calls on a typical weekday at any one stop with a current timetable within a 400 m walk of the place, along mapped roads. It is a rough sign of how often vehicles come. 0 means there is no such stop within a 400 m walk.
definition: For each place, the largest value of trips_weekday (see transit.stop_trips_weekday) among the scheduled stops whose operator's feed has not ended on the as-of date and whose walking distance from the place (see tw_m) is 400 m or less, or 0 when there is none. It is ts_calls with the stops chosen by walking instead of a straight line. A place listed in tw_straight keeps its ts_calls. A stop with 20 or more calls is a frequent stop in the observatory's access classes; 20 is a threshold chosen for the observatory, not a standard. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to 0 (none), 1 (1 to 19) or 20 (20 or more), the classes the access shares read (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
